name: GitHub Copilot Memory (agentic memory)
description: Repository-scoped memories that Copilot coding agent, code review and CLI write automatically, share across features, validate against the current code before use, and expire after 28 days; owners can review/delete them.
launch_date: 2026-01-15 (public preview); on by default for Pro/Pro+ 2026-03-04
traction: Shipped to all paid GitHub Copilot plans; default-on for Pro/Pro+
notes: Catalog has 'GitHub Copilot custom instructions' (static file) but not this learned-memory feature.

name: OpenAI Codex Memories + Chronicle
description: Codex Memories carries preferences, conventions and pitfalls across Codex threads as local Markdown files; Chronicle (research preview) adds screen-aware memory by having background agents summarize periodic Mac screen captures into those memory files.
traction: OpenAI first-party feature for Codex app (ChatGPT Pro, macOS at launch); wide press coverage
notes: Primary URL is the Codex developer hub; the article sources were the pages opened. Distinct from catalog 'OpenAI Codex CLI' / 'AGENTS.md'.

name: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service Memory
description: Fully managed long-term memory store built into Azure/Microsoft Foundry Agent Service that extracts user-profile facts and chat summaries and retrieves them across sessions — Microsoft's peer to AgentCore Memory and Vertex Memory Bank.
traction: Major-vendor launch (Microsoft Ignite 2025); InfoQ coverage Feb 2026
notes: Catalog's 'Microsoft Copilot Memory' covers M365 Copilot, not the developer platform.

name: OpenViking (ByteDance Volcengine)
description: Open-source 'context database' from ByteDance's Volcengine that unifies agent memory, RAG knowledge and skills behind a virtual filesystem (viking:// URIs) with tiered loading and self-evolving context.
traction: ~39k GitHub stars; #6 on GitHub agent-memory topic; listed #3 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory products

name: Hermes Agent memory (Nous Research)
description: Nous Research's open-source self-improving agent keeps an agent-curated MEMORY.md/USER.md notebook injected at session start, FTS5 search over past sessions with LLM summarisation, and optional Honcho user modelling.
traction: ~254k GitHub stars; one of the most-starred agent projects of 2026

name: OpenClaw memory
description: Memory system of the viral OpenClaw personal agent: plain Markdown files (USER.md, MEMORY.md, daily memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md notes, DREAMS.md) with memory_search/memory_get tools, automatic pre-compaction flush and a 'dreaming' sweep that distils daily notes into long-term memory; pluggable engines (LanceDB, Honcho, wiki).
traction: ~392k GitHub stars; spawned an ecosystem of memory plugins (memory-lancedb-pro, gbrain, MemClaw)

name: Perplexity Brain
description: Topic-organised shared memory layer under Perplexity Search, the Computer agent and possibly Comet; stores projects, decisions and sources, retrieves selectively per task, and exposes topics plus a 3D connection map to the user.
traction: Major-vendor announcement; Perplexity claims +25% correctness, +16% recall, -13% cost on context-dependent tasks
notes: Could be merged as an update into catalog's 'Perplexity Memory'; listed separately because it is a new agent-level system.

name: Cursor Memories
description: Project-scoped memories in Cursor, created either by a background 'sidecar' model watching chats or by the agent via tool calls, and managed as auto-generated rules in settings.
traction: First-party feature of one of the most widely used AI IDEs
notes: Catalog has 'Cursor Rules' and 'Cursor (IDE)', but not the learned Memories feature.

name: Gemini CLI memory (save_memory / GEMINI.md)
description: Google's open-source Gemini CLI persists facts by editing tiered Markdown memory files — repo GEMINI.md, a per-project private memory folder and global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md — that load into hierarchical context each session.
traction: Google first-party; Gemini CLI is one of the most-used terminal coding agents

name: TencentDB Agent Memory
description: Tencent's team-level memory hub that turns conversations, docs and code into four reusable memory assets: chat memory, skills, an LLM-wiki and a code graph.
traction: ~30k GitHub stars; big-tech vendor

name: gbrain (Garry Tan)
description: Open-source agent 'brain' storing explicit sourced facts with corrections and withdrawals, shared across agents; built as the memory for OpenClaw/Hermes agents.
traction: ~31k GitHub stars; author is YC CEO; listed #6 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory

name: agentmemory (rohitg00)
description: Self-hosted persistent memory layer that captures coding-agent activity and recalls it in later sessions, positioned on public benchmark results.
traction: ~29k GitHub stars; #7 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory

name: Beads (Steve Yegge)
description: Dolt-backed, dependency-aware graph issue tracker that acts as persistent structured memory for coding agents, replacing markdown plans; `bd remember` stores durable facts and `bd prime` re-injects them.
traction: ~28k GitHub stars

name: memU (NevaMind)
description: Lightweight agent memory system that builds a shared, file-like 'memory wiki' across sessions, agents and devices and can extract reusable skills from agent history; also offered as a hosted service (memu.pro).
traction: ~14k stars; #9 on GitHub agent-memory topic

name: Honcho (Plastic Labs)
description: Memory library/service for stateful agents that reasons over stored messages to build 'peer' representations (theory-of-mind style user models) queryable via a dialectic API; used as Hermes Agent's and OpenClaw's user-modelling backend.
traction: ~7.7k stars; integrated into Hermes Agent and OpenClaw; public evals at evals.honcho.dev

name: context-mode
description: MCP server + hooks that sandbox tool output out of the coding agent's context window (claims ~98% reduction) and persist session memory across 17 agent platforms.
traction: ~32k GitHub stars

name: Serena (Oraios)
description: LSP-backed MCP coding toolkit ('IDE for your agent') with a built-in project memory system for sharing knowledge across sessions, users and projects alongside AGENTS.md.
traction: ~30k GitHub stars

name: Screenpipe
description: Local-first 24/7 screen and audio recorder that indexes what you see/hear and exposes it as context/memory to AI agents (MCP, API); open-source Rewind/Recall alternative.
traction: ~22k GitHub stars; Y Combinator S26

name: Second Me (Mindverse)
description: Open-source system for training a local 'AI self' from your own notes and memories using hierarchical memory modelling, deployable as a personal agent on a network of Second Mes.
traction: ~15.7k GitHub stars; #12 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory

name: ACE — Agentic Context Engineering
section: Recent method papers — theorized, no distinct product
description: Treats context and agent memory as an evolving 'playbook' that a generate→reflect→curate loop updates incrementally, avoiding brevity bias and context collapse. Reports +10.6% on agent benchmarks and matches the top AppWorld production agent.
traction: ICLR 2026; Stanford/SambaNova; popular community implementation (kayba-ai ACE ~2.5k stars)
notes: Catalog has generic 'Context Engineering' and 'Dynamic Cheatsheet' but not ACE. Its kayba-ai productization could go under Dedicated memory layers.

name: HaluMem
description: Benchmark that measures hallucination at each stage of an agent memory system (extraction, updating, QA) rather than only final answers; HaluMem-Medium/Long datasets have ~15k memory points and contexts over 1M tokens.
traction: From MemTensor and China Telecom; HF dataset IAAR-Shanghai/HaluMem; widely cited by memory vendors

name: BEAM (Beyond a Million Tokens) + LIGHT
description: ICLR 2026 benchmark of 100 coherent conversations up to 10M tokens with 2,000 validated probes across ten memory abilities, including contradiction resolution and event ordering. It also proposes the LIGHT episodic/working/scratchpad memory method.
traction: ICLR 2026 paper; Mem0 publishes BEAM explainer and results

name: SimpleMem
section: Recent method papers — theorized, no distinct product
description: Efficient lifelong memory built from semantic structured compression into self-contained facts, online synthesis of related facts and intent-aware multi-index retrieval. Reports +26% F1 over Mem0 on LoCoMo with ~30x fewer tokens.
traction: ~3.8k stars; ICML 2026; UNC/Berkeley/UCSC

name: Letta Code
description: Letta's stateful coding-agent harness: agents rewrite their own memory blocks and skills, version context in git via MemFS (syncable to GitHub) and reflect via a periodic /sleeptime 'dreaming' process.
traction: ~3.5k stars; from Letta (MemGPT) team
notes: Catalog has 'Letta / MemGPT' (platform) but not the coding-agent harness.

name: Basic Memory
description: Local-first MCP memory where each memory is a Markdown note with observations and wikilink relations that form a traversable knowledge graph, indexed with SQLite (optional Postgres vectors), plus an optional hosted cloud.
traction: ~3.6k stars; widely used MCP memory server with a paid cloud tier

name: Evo-Memory
description: Google streaming benchmark for test-time learning: agents must search, adapt and update memory across task sequences. It implements 10+ memory modules on 10 datasets and introduces the ExpRAG and ReMem baselines.
traction: Google (Ed Chi, Fernando Pereira et al.) authorship

name: STALE (+ CUPMEM)
description: Conflict/update benchmark of 400 scenarios with 1,200 queries (up to ~150K tokens) testing whether agents notice that later facts implicitly invalidate earlier memories; the best model scores 55.2%. The CUPMEM prototype adds write-time state adjudication.
traction: Directly targets implicit memory conflict; HKUST/Wuhan/CUHK
notes: No code link was found in the abstract.

name: MemConflict
description: Diagnostic benchmark covering dynamic, static and conditional memory conflicts, with black-box answer and white-box retrieval/ranking metrics; it evaluates A-Mem, LangMem, Letta, MemOS, Mem0 and Memobase.
traction: Head-to-head evaluation of six named memory systems; Renmin Univ + MemTensor

name: Redis Agent Memory Server
description: Redis's official working + long-term memory server for agents (REST and MCP), with automatic extraction, semantic search and topic/entity tagging; also used to give Snowflake Cortex Agents persistent memory.
traction: Major infrastructure vendor's official memory server; Redis-Snowflake integration blog
notes: Few stars, but included because it comes from a major vendor.

name: MemoryBear
description: Open-source memory system modelled on human cognition, with perception, extraction, association and forgetting stages; also offered as a hosted product.
traction: ~6.5k stars; #18 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory

name: Neo4j Agent Memory (Neo4j Labs)
description: Neo4j Labs' graph-native agent memory library (Python and TypeScript) that stores conversations, builds knowledge/context graphs and records agent reasoning traces to learn from.
traction: Official vendor-lab project; packages published on PyPI and npm

name: EvoMemBench
description: Benchmark that crosses memory scope (in-episode vs cross-episode) with content (knowledge vs execution) and compares 15 memory methods with long-context baselines under one protocol.
traction: Standardized comparison of 15 memory methods; HKUST(GZ) and others

name: memory-lancedb-pro (OpenClaw plugin)
description: Enhanced LanceDB memory plugin for OpenClaw that adds hybrid vector + BM25 retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, multi-scope isolation and a management CLI.
traction: ~4.5k stars; #21 in TeleAI Awesome-Agent-Memory

name: m_flow (M-Flow)
description: Cognitive memory engine modelled on biology that presents itself as a new paradigm for graph RAG for agents.
traction: ~4.5k stars; #13 on GitHub agent-memory topic

name: Acontext (memodb)
description: 'Agent Skills as a Memory Layer': an open-source skill-memory layer that stores what agents learn as agent skill files. Built by the Memobase team.
traction: ~3.7k stars

name: memsearch (Zilliz)
description: Zilliz's persistent memory layer shared across agents like Claude Code and Codex: Markdown files are the source of truth, and Milvus indexes them for search.
traction: ~2.7k stars; from the Milvus vendor

name: Memory-R1
section: Recent method papers — theorized, no distinct product
description: Uses RL (PPO/GRPO) to train a Memory Manager that learns ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP operations and an Answer Agent that filters retrieved memories. Beats heuristic memory baselines on LoCoMo, MSC and LongMemEval from just 152 training QA pairs.
traction: ACL 2026 long paper; LMU/Oxford/TUM; widely cited RL-for-memory work
notes: No official code link on the ACL page. Check before listing as code-released.

name: Sleep-time Compute (Letta)
section: Recent method papers — theorized, no distinct product
description: Agents use idle time to reorganize and pre-reason over stored context ('learned context'). Letta ships this as sleep-time agents (v0.7.0+), where a background agent manages the primary agent's core memory.
traction: Shipped in Letta 0.7.0 and Letta Code (/sleeptime); arXiv 2504.13171
notes: Pre-2026, but it underpins the 2026 'dreaming' consolidation trend (Claude Auto Dream, OpenClaw DREAMS.md). arXiv page was blocked from fetch.

name: CORE (RedPlanet)
description: Always-on 'personal AI OS' that indexes email, meetings, GitHub, Linear, Slack and assistant chats into a temporal knowledge graph with fact classification and intent-driven retrieval, plus MCP integrations.
traction: ~2k stars; reports 88.24% on LoCoMo (vendor claim)

name: Memanto (Moorcheh)
description: A 'memory agent' that manages other agents' memories, deciding what to keep, what conflicts, what expires and who needs to know; runs locally (Docker/Ollama) or as a free cloud.
traction: ~2.2k stars; self-reported 89.8% LongMemEval / 87.1% LoCoMo
